didBVerificationMethod: public metadata only: directory listing, public_did from local-install.json, locally recomputed sha256 of that public DID, and the opaque sha256 of identity.dpapi
distinctnessBasis: distinct public did:key values (canonical_did derives the identifier from public-key material) plus distinct opaque identity.dpapi ciphertext digests
custodyModel: canonical-local-agent DPAPIKeyProvider, Ed25519 private key protected per-file by Windows DPAPI under a TrustedPaths state root; key never leaves the local machine and is never exported
roleBasis: adopted TCLK d48e873 dist/frames.js enforces accept.from != offer.from; dist/machine.js restricts lock and refund to the payer and reveal to the payee
didAUnchangedMethod: sha256 of opaque identity.dpapi ciphertext plus size/mtime, and of nonces.json, operator.json and local-install.json, compared against the digest recorded before the human enrollment; DPAPI protect() is randomized so any rewrite changes the ciphertext digest

custodyIsolationProbe.storage: throwaway temp directory, removed after the run
custodyIsolationProbe.identitiesCreated: two disposable fixture keys, no operator enrollment

limitations: DID B now exists and is cryptographically distinct from DID A, but both are controlled by ONE human operator, on one Windows account, on one machine. This is not two humans, not two organizations, not two independent economic counterparties, not two wallet owners, not evidence of payment or settlement, and not FLOP eligibility.

Verification used public metadata only: directory entries, the public did:key from local-install.json, a locally recomputed sha256 of that public DID, and the opaque sha256 of identity.dpapi. Neither protected blob was unprotected and no private-key bytes were read, derived, compared, exported or printed.

Distinct ciphertext digests do not by themselves prove distinct plaintext keys. The distinct did:key values do, because canonical_did derives the identifier from public-key material; the ciphertext digests only corroborate that two separate protected blobs exist.

No signature was produced for DID B. A did:key is derived from public-key material alone, so a working DID B signing path is unproven and belongs to the Phase 3B execution path with its own durable one-shot budget.

Role binding is protocol role assignment only. It satisfies the adopted TCLK state machine's DID-role separation; it proves nothing about economic independence, wallet ownership, payment or settlement.
Storage separation was observed at one instant from filesystem paths and digests. It is not a live tamper guarantee and must be re-checked before any public write.
DID A immutability is proved by digest comparison against the value recorded in Phase 3B.C1a, not by any inspection of key material.
nextRecommendedAction: Phase 3B.1 — freeze the one-deal public manifest against these two verified DIDs and their frozen roles, with no signing, no nonce reservation and no Technocore access
